1. S6? ruling — ACCEPT the reduction to S1

ACCEPT:

S6? World/Locus birth uniqueness
    ↓
S1(domain = World locus-birth/currentness)

The experiment materially improves the claim.

Against the frozen cd-core API, two births of the same LocusId under one WorldRoot:

  • both begin;

  • both attach different carriers;

  • both execute authority-bearing detach transitions;

  • both histories individually audit under the same root;

  • a warden minted by birth A can finalize birth B's live attachment.

That last witness is particularly strong: the existing per-birth capability vocabulary cannot distinguish the two births because the birth domain itself was never admitted.

The scratch WorldAdmission remedy has S1's shape:

one linear admission value for the domain
consumed by every birth
duplicate birth refused
failure returns the admission for retry
reuse refused by the type system

The properties left open by the remedy are already classified elsewhere:

durability / copy / restart of WorldAdmission -> S3
cross-world ID collision                      -> representation / identity

I do not see a residual semantic property that requires a distinct S6.

Required package change

The current frontier should no longer be described as:

six semantic obligations S1–S6?

Use:

five working semantic obligations S1–S5
+
S1 scoped corollaries, including World locus-birth/currentness

No claim is made that S1–S5 are an irreducible complete basis.

2. EXP-4 finality/liveness gap — REAL, but do not create S6/S7

EXP-4 surfaced a genuine missing dimension:

what guarantees progress when the current holder becomes permanently unavailable?

S1–S5 are overwhelmingly safety / integrity obligations. None says a nonterminal Locus must ever make progress after holder loss.

That is not evidence for another safety invariant.

Create a separate liveness axis.

Recommended working candidate:

L1 — Recoverable succession / explicit terminalization

For a Locus whose policy declares continued service,
if the current holder becomes permanently unavailable and sufficient
admissible loss evidence is eventually established, the system eventually:

    A. admits exactly one successor in a later generation,
       OR
    B. moves the Locus to an explicit terminal/quarantined state.

It must not remain silently ambiguous forever.

Important:

  • L1 is profile/policy-scoped.

  • A system may intentionally choose halt-on-loss and therefore not promise succession.

  • L1 must not weaken S1 to obtain progress.

  • Warden/finality machinery appears to be one implementation of this liveness cost.

  • Do not promote L1 as irreducible yet.

Recommended registry treatment:

semantic_safety: S1–S5
semantic_liveness: L1? ...

Do not mix them merely to preserve one numbered table.

3. EXP-1 ARM B ruling — TESTED under the narrow trust profile, not a broad cross-host theorem

The ARM B receipts are strong for what they actually test.

Both winner orderings satisfy:

exactly_one_advance            true
refusal_names_mechanism        true
witness_head_binds_winner      true
loser_quarantined_at_reopen    true

The crash matrix also shows the witness CAS placement is compatible with the tested local roll-forward protocol.

Therefore I accept:

S3 currentness is TESTED under a single correct, available, linearizable witness for two independently copied controller/store namespaces.

I do not accept the unqualified phrase:

S3 cross-host: TESTED

because the reported "host 2" is a container on the same PX13 physical machine, using host networking, and the witness is also on that machine.

This is a good distributed-protocol experiment, but it has not tested:

  • two physical machines;

  • network partition between controller and witness;

  • witness crash/restart during competing admission;

  • witness durable-storage corruption;

  • witness failover;

  • quorum disagreement;

  • physical-host failure independence.

Correct evidence language

Prefer:

TESTED:
    two-controller / two-filesystem-namespace copied-world topology,
    single correct and available witness

SUPPORTED by mechanism shape:
    cross-machine safety under the same witness assumptions

UNTESTED:
    failure-tolerant / partition-tolerant distributed witness service

A quorum witness is not required to establish safety under the explicit single-witness trust profile.

A quorum/replicated witness is required before claiming fault-tolerant availability or a realistic distributed-currentness service.

ARM B already demonstrates the semantic point:

moving the authoritative currentness CAS outside both copies can prevent both descendants from advancing.

That is enough for this R10-pre reduction.

4. E-13 / E-14 / E-15 — current live_local language is too generous

E-13 — exclusivity outside the copyable store

At efa8881, F31 demonstrates:

Root::lock_path(path) = "{caller-chosen-root}.lock"

Copying the root to another pathname creates another lock namespace and therefore another current controller for the same Locus.

That falsifies the broad intended mechanism:

the currentness anchor is outside the claimant-copyable / claimant-selectable namespace.

Same-path locking still works. But that is a narrower fact.

Recommended split:

E-13a same-anchor incarnation exclusivity
    TESTED / live_local
    scope: one canonical lock object / namespace

E-13b canonical host-local Locus currentness anchor
    FALSIFIED at efa8881 by F31
    R0.8.4 repair may close it, but this package does not contain
    the full R0.8.4 source+receipt needed to adjudicate that closure

E-13c witnessed multi-namespace currentness
    TESTED under the ARM-B single-witness profile

Do not let live_local (narrowed) obscure that the original load-bearing claim failed under a pathname-copy attack.

E-14 — root commitment under injective encoding

F23/F24 show that the committed material was not injective over the semantic interpretation of the SQLite store:

  • schema/collation can change reads without changing covered row values;

  • a trigger can mutate semantics from inside the honest writer transaction;

  • unordered reads can change authority resolution while the digest is unchanged.

Therefore the broad E-14 mechanism is not live_local under the attacker-writable-store threat profile.

Correct classification:

TESTED-CONDITIONAL:
    row-value commitment under a fixed/trusted SQLite interpretation contract

FALSIFIED / OPEN:
    semantic-store commitment when schema/interpreter metadata is attacker-modifiable

If the SQLite schema is part of the attacker-writable database, calling it "trusted" simply moves the open obligation into the trust profile; it does not close S3.

E-15 — mutation-time canonicality

F23's trigger case also weakens E-15.

The transaction may be serialized correctly while an attacker-installed schema trigger changes canonical rows from inside that same transaction.

Therefore E-15 should also say:

TESTED under fixed/trusted schema/interpreter

until schema semantics are committed/verified.

5. PX13 R0.8.3 ruling

I accept the following distinction:

R0.8.3 execution happened:               YES
21-run series was reported green:        YES
historical receipt should be preserved:  YES
R0.8 semantic layer may freeze:           NO

The green series does not imply all its claims were actually measured.

F25 is especially important:

a control ran, but never reached the subject it claimed to attack.

That means:

PASS != evidence
unless the control is capable of producing FAIL for the claimed defect.

This should become a general factory requirement.

Recommended meta-rule:

FAC-CONTROL-SENSITIVITY

Every negative control used to support an evidence-class promotion must
carry either:

    A. a demonstrated pre-fix / injected-fault FAIL,
    OR
    B. an independently witnessed mutation showing the control reaches
       the claimed subject and distinguishes the forbidden state.

A green-only control with no demonstrated failure sensitivity cannot
promote a semantic claim.

This may be more important than any single R0.8 patch.

F22/F23/F25/F31 are not reasons to discard the R0.8 work. They are exactly the reason the execution round was valuable.

7. EXP-5 authority merge — split the result instead of assigning all of it to S2

The experiment is useful and the core reworded rule survives:

do not blindly union effective authority; use a proven join-safe representation or merge evidence and rederive.

But E-46 currently groups three different phenomena:

A. Revoked/spent authority resurrected by union

This is an S2 non-amplification / current-authority problem.

Good S2 evidence.

B. Grants from separate replicas combine into a conjunction neither replica locally held

This is not automatically authority amplification.

If both grants are globally valid and the policy intentionally allows conjunction, then the merged authority is justified by two admitted grant chains.

The real question is whether the policy/merge contract permits composition, not whether one replica previously held the conjunction.

Do not use this witness by itself as evidence of S2 failure.

C. A stale copied Authority value acts after revocation

That is S1 at the action target / consumption point.

Therefore split E-46 conceptually:

merge representation law / join-safety     -> CROSS / representation
revocation or one-shot resurrection         -> S2
stale-true action after snapshot             -> S1

This will keep the cross-registry map from making S2 absorb every authority-related phenomenon.

13. Final ruling

The execution round succeeded at its real purpose: it changed the map.

Most important results:

  1. S6 collapses to S1 under real cd-core execution.

  2. Locus does not reduce to authority, and EXP-4 identifies history/provenance/custody/finality residue.

  3. A distinct liveness axis is now visible.

  4. Side-effecting observation is write-mediated in the tested TRVM path.

  5. Blind authority union fails on real APIs; join-safe representation and action admission are separate concerns.

  6. A single external witness can enforce both S3 currentness/history obligations for competing copies under its explicit trust profile.

  7. R0.8.3's green series exposed controls that could not fail, validating the rule that receipts themselves require adversarial sensitivity.

  8. R0.8 remains OPEN because currentness anchor identity, SQLite interpretation commitment, and filesystem-root trust are still load-bearing.

GO to codebase iteration.

Do not return to Fable for another broad invariant-search round.
